documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46M here to establish. Previous PCP office closing adult panel; records requested.

HTN since ~2014, on lisinopril 10 mg for years, no side effects. Doesn't check at home.
Gout since ~2016, a few flares before allopurinol. On allopurinol 300 mg daily since, no flare in over a year. No colchicine at home.
No surgeries. NKDA.

FH: father with HTN, paternal uncle with gout, mother hypothyroid.
SH: married. Works at a battery recycling plant as a technician, long time in plant work. Quit cigarettes about 5 yrs ago. 2-3 beers a week. Rides his road bike most weekends in season.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: BP 136/86, recheck similar. Well appearing. TMs normal. Neck no thyromegaly. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abd benign. Joints: no tophi, no synovitis. Ext without edema. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P
1. HTN, near goal on lisinopril 10. Continue. Encouraged home cuff.
2. Gout, quiet on allopurinol 300. Uric acid today.
3. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, uric acid; one-time hep C and HIV, he agrees. Tdap given today. Colon screening is due at 45 now; discussed, he'd rather wait until spring. Flu shot in October.
4. Former smoker, light.

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Occupational Medicine Consultation: hearing
documents.author: occupational medicine
documents.body:
OCCUPATIONAL MEDICINE CLINIC
Date of service: 02/09/2022
Re: Craig Abbott, DOB 08/09/1973
Referred by: employer hearing conservation program after a shift on his annual audiogram

Mr. Abbott is a 48-year-old battery recycling technician, about 25 years in plant work, who has noticed hearing getting worse over the past several months, mostly trouble following conversation on the floor and in restaurants. No otalgia, no drainage, no dizziness or spinning. No tinnitus complaints today.
History: hypertension and gout. Meds: lisinopril, allopurinol 300 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father hypertension, paternal uncle gout, mother hypothyroidism.

Exam: vital signs normal. Ear canals clear. Tympanic membranes intact on both sides, pearly, no fluid or redness. Weber goes to the right. Rinne positive bilaterally, air conduction better than bone.
Audiogram today (attached): high-frequency sensorineural loss both ears with a notch at 4 kHz, left a little worse.

Assessment: Noise-induced hearing loss, bilateral, work-related.
Plan: Fitted for foam plugs plus earmuffs for loud areas. Repeat audiogram yearly through the employer program. Not at a level needing amplification at present.

Occupational Medicine Physician
cc: primary care

documents.title: Occupational Medicine Visit: weakness and abdominal pain
documents.author: occupational medicine
documents.body:
OCCUPATIONAL MEDICINE CLINIC
Date of service: 08/10/2022, with addendum 08/12/2022
Re: Craig Abbott, DOB 08/09/1973

Seen previously here in February for work-related hearing loss. Now 49, he comes back with roughly half a year of slowly increasing weakness in both hands and both feet, tiredness through the whole shift, and crampy belly pain. In the last few weeks he has also become constipated, and store-bought laxatives have done nothing.
He works the battery breaking and smelting side of the recycling plant.
PMH: hypertension, gout, noise-induced hearing loss. Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, allopurinol 300 mg daily. NKDA.
Family history unchanged from February.

Exam: BP 145/90. Mildly pale conjunctivae. Abdomen soft. Light touch and pinprick reduced in both hands to the wrists and both feet to above the ankles. Strength mildly reduced in grip.

Labs today: Hgb 10.2, MCV 74, creatinine 1.8, BUN 29, uric acid 8.5. Smear shows basophilic stippling.
Addendum 8/12: blood lead 72 mcg/dL.

Assessment: Symptomatic occupational lead poisoning with anemia, peripheral neuropathy, abdominal symptoms and reduced kidney function.
Plan:
1. Medical removal from all lead-exposed tasks effective now; employer notified per standard.
2. Oral succimer 10 mg/kg (900 mg) three times daily for 5 days, then twice daily for 14 days. Started 8/12.
3. Blood lead and CBC after the course and then at intervals per surveillance.
4. Please follow blood pressure, kidney function and gout.

Occupational Medicine Physician
cc: primary care

Kidney number up to 1.8 from 1.1 last fall; told him that's part of the lead effect and we will watch it. Visit booked mid-September. Advised to avoid NSAIDs and keep up fluids.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
49M with HTN, gout, noise-induced hearing loss and occupational lead poisoning (occ med, Aug 2022), back to go over symptoms that are hanging on.

Subjective: Still worn out by mid-afternoon. Belly aches most days, dull and all over, and he is constipated, a BM every 3-4 days despite fiber. Hands and feet tingle on and off, and they feel weak when he grips tools or climbs stairs. No weight loss, no blood in stool, no fevers. Still off the lead side at the plant since August, no other exposures at home that he knows of (no remodeling, no firearms, no hobby casting).
Meds: allopurinol 300 daily, lisinopril 10 daily. Succimer finished 9/2022. NKDA.
FH: father HTN, paternal uncle gout, mother hypothyroidism.

Objective: vitals as charted. Looks pale. Abdomen with mild diffuse tenderness, no rebound, no guarding, no masses. Neuro: light touch decreased in both hands and both feet in a glove-and-stocking distribution; reflexes present.

Labs 2/6: Hgb 10.2, MCV 74, Cr 1.8, BUN 29, uric acid 9.5. Smear: basophilic stippling. Ferritin 140, so not iron deficiency. Blood lead 44 (down from 72, but up from what occ med expected after chelation).

A/P
1. Lead poisoning with persistent anemia, neuropathy, abdominal symptoms and reduced kidney function. Numbers unchanged in 6 months; lead level consistent with release from bone stores. Will call occ med today to share and coordinate on whether more chelation is needed. Must stay out of lead work.
2. Constipation from #1: more fluids and dietary fiber.
3. Gout: uric acid 9.5 on allopurinol 300; no flares.
4. HTN: continue lisinopril 10.
Recheck CBC, BMP, lead in 3 months.

documents.title: Call with occupational medicine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with his occupational medicine physician. Their view: rebound after a single course is expected, level is falling, no repeat chelation unless it climbs back over 50 or symptoms worsen. He stays on permanent removal for now with their surveillance draws. Agreed. Pt updated by phone; he's relieved there's no more of the capsules.

PREVENTIVE MEDICINE, EMPLOYER HEALTH SCREENING PROGRAM
Date of service: 08/14/2024
Patient: Craig Abbott, DOB 08/09/1973

Scheduled visit to go over this year's occupational screening and his heart risk.
Background: hypertension, gout, work-related noise-induced hearing loss, occupational lead poisoning in 2022 now off lead tasks.
Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily, allopurinol 300 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: technician at a battery recycling plant. Stopped smoking 10 years ago. Alcohol socially, 2 to 3 drinks weekly.

Screening results:
- Blood lead 16 mcg/dL, continuing to fall.
- Creatinine 1.4.
- Audiogram unchanged from 2022.

Cardiovascular risk: pooled cohort 10-year ASCVD estimate 6.8% (borderline). Explained in plain numbers what that estimate means: out of 100 men like him, about 7 would be expected to have a heart attack or stroke in 10 years.
Recommendations: no statin at this time; Mediterranean-style eating, keep up cycling, limit alcohol. Continue care with primary care for blood pressure and gout. Annual screening next year.

Preventive Medicine Physician

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast
reports.text:
Technique: helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without oral or IV contrast, renal stone protocol.
Findings: 4 mm calculus in the left distal ureter about 2 cm above the ureterovesical junction, low attenuation (approximately 420 HU), not seen on the scout image. No hydronephrosis. Kidneys normal in size with no additional calculi. Right ureter and bladder unremarkable. Liver, spleen, pancreas and adrenals unremarkable. No free fluid. Appendix normal. Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: 4 mm left distal ureteral calculus, low density, suggestive of uric acid composition. No hydronephrosis.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, REGIONAL HOSPITAL
Arrival 01/31/2026 09:40. Received by primary care 02/03/2026.
Pt: Craig Abbott, 52M. Allergies: NKDA.

HPI: Sharp pain in the left side that came on suddenly this morning and hasn't let up, with nausea, no vomiting. Can't get comfortable, keeps changing position on the stretcher. No injury, no recent illness. Rode an organized cycling event in hot weather last weekend on a trip south. First time with pain like this. No burning with urination, no penile discharge.
PMH: HTN, gout, occupational lead poisoning (followed by occupational medicine and PCP), noise-induced hearing loss. Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, allopurinol 300 mg daily.
FH: father HTN, paternal uncle gout, mother hypothyroidism.
SH: former smoker, social alcohol, battery recycling technician. Eats a lot of red meat and seafood.

Triage: HR 108, BP 166/98, afebrile, SpO2 98% RA. Pain 9/10.
Exam: uncomfortable, writhing. Left CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft, no peritoneal signs. No testicular tenderness.

UA: many RBCs (>50/hpf), pH 5.0, no bacteria, no casts, nitrite and LE negative.
Cr 1.4 (baseline per records 1.3-1.4). WBC normal. Uric acid 8.9.
CT A/P without contrast: 4 mm left distal ureteral stone, low density, no hydronephrosis.

ED course: IV fluids, IV acetaminophen, IV ondansetron. Pain improved to 5/10, recurred.

Disposition: placed in observation for pain control and stone passage; strain all urine.

documents.title: Observation Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL, OBSERVATION UNIT
Admit 01/31/2026, discharge 02/01/2026.
Patient: Craig Abbott, DOB 08/09/1973. Allergies: NKDA.
Reason for observation: left renal colic from a 4 mm distal ureteral stone.
Course: oral fluids and IV fluids overnight, tamsulosin started, acetaminophen and ondansetron. Passed a small stone into the strainer at 05:20 on 2/1 with prompt relief. Sent for analysis. Eating and voiding normally; pain 0/10 at discharge.
Discharge diagnosis: left distal ureterolithiasis, stone passed.
Discharge medications: tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily x14 days (may stop sooner since stone passed), ondansetron 4 mg ODT q8h prn, acetaminophen 1000 mg q6h prn. Continue lisinopril 10 mg and allopurinol 300 mg.
Follow-up: primary care within 1-2 weeks; stone analysis to be forwarded.
Hospitalist

documents.title: Follow-up after ED / observation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED 1/31 for L renal colic, observation overnight, passed a 4 mm stone 2/1. Analysis: 100% uric acid.
Feels completely fine. No flank pain, no blood in urine, no fever. Stopped tamsulosin yesterday.
Admits he eats red meat or shellfish most days and doesn't drink much water on shift. Gout: no flares.
Meds: lisinopril 10, allopurinol 300. NKDA.

Exam: BP above goal. No CVA tenderness. Abd soft, NT.
Reviewed ED labs: Cr 1.4 (his baseline), uric acid 8.9, urine pH 5.0.

A/P
1. Uric acid ureteral stone, passed. Acidic urine and uric acid above goal both favor recurrence. Start potassium citrate 10 mEq BID to bring urine pH up; he'll check urine pH strips at home, aiming for 6-6.5. Fluids at least 2.5 L/day. Cut back red meat and seafood.
2. Gout / hyperuricemia: increase allopurinol to 400 mg daily (100 mg tabs x4), target uric acid under 6.
3. HTN: on lisinopril with new potassium citrate, will check potassium and creatinine in 3 months.
4. Lead poisoning, stable.
RTC 3 months with uric acid, BMP.

documents.title: Prior authorization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy reports insurer needs prior authorization for potassium citrate ER. Submitted with diagnosis of uric acid ureteral stone and urine pH 5.0. Approved same afternoon for 12 months. Pharmacy notified; allopurinol 100 mg tabs filled without issue.

documents.title: Urine strips

documents.body: Doing the pH strips in the morning. Mostly 6.0, a couple 6.5. Water bottle at work now. Taking the 4 small allopurinols, no issues. That ok?

documents.title: RE: Urine strips
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's right where we want it. Keep going and we'll check blood work in May.

No further colic or hematuria. Urine pH 6-6.5 at home. Drinking 2.5-3 L. Fewer steaks; still likes seafood. No gout.
Meds: lisinopril 10, allopurinol 400 (100 x4), potassium citrate 10 mEq BID. NKDA.
Labs 5/11: uric acid 6.4, K 4.6, Cr 1.3.
Exam: BP above goal. No edema.
A/P: Uric acid stone, no recurrence on potassium citrate. K fine with lisinopril. Uric acid improving, near goal on 400 mg. Continue all. HTN unchanged. Recheck in 3 months.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, turning 53 this week.
No kidney stone symptoms since February. Urine pH strips 6.0-6.5. No gout flares. Riding a lot this summer and carrying extra water. Toes fine except in the cold.
Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, allopurinol 400 mg daily, potassium citrate 10 mEq twice daily. NKDA.
Home BP log averages ~140/88.

Exam: BP above goal, similar on recheck. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No CVA tenderness. No edema. No tophi.

A/P
1. Uric acid nephrolithiasis history: no recurrence. Continue potassium citrate and fluids.
2. Gout: allopurinol 400, uric acid today.
3. HTN: continue lisinopril 10.
4. Lead poisoning: blood lead with today's draw.
BMP, CBC, uric acid, lead. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All back. Uric acid 5.8, finally under 6. Lead 8. Potassium, kidney function and blood count all steady. Keep doing what you're doing.
